config.defaultShell.description: Path to the shell used for new sessions. Leave empty to use your login shell. Machine scope: a workspace cannot override it.
config.startupCommands.description: Commands sent to the shell in order right after a session is created. Machine scope: a workspace cannot override it.
config.confirmOpenLink.description: Show a confirmation dialog before opening a terminal link with Cmd / Ctrl + click.
config.showResourceStats.description: Show saved-image size and extension host memory in the view toolbar. The memory figure covers the whole extension host process, which is shared with every other extension.
config.restoreScrollback.description: Keep the scrollback of each terminal on disk so it can be read again after the editor restarts. The shell itself is not restored. Machine scope: a workspace cannot override it.
config.rendererType.description: How the terminal is drawn. `auto` uses the GPU renderer when it is available and falls back to the DOM renderer otherwise.
renderer.auto: (Recommended) Use the GPU renderer when available, otherwise the DOM renderer
renderer.webgl: Always request the GPU renderer (still falls back to the DOM renderer if it cannot start)
config.themePreset.description: Terminal theme for Terminal 1. Also selectable inside the Terminal For AI CLI view.
config.themePresetSecondary.description: Terminal theme for Terminal 2. Empty means it follows Terminal 1. Also selectable inside the Terminal For AI CLI view.
theme.inherit: Use the same theme as Terminal 1
theme.modern: (Recommended) Muted colors that blend with the VS Code theme
theme.basic: Plain classic terminal: white on black
theme.clearDark: Dark background with soft cyan text
theme.clearLight: Light background with dark grey text
theme.homebrew: Homebrew style: neon green on black
theme.manPage: Man-page style: pale background, dark text
walkthrough.setup.title: Get Started with Terminal For AI CLI
walkthrough.setup.description: Put the terminal beside your code, then start your first session.
walkthrough.setup.move.title: Move the terminal to the Secondary Side Bar
walkthrough.setup.move.description:
The view starts in the Activity Bar, where it covers the file tree. Moving it to the Secondary Side Bar puts the terminal beside your code instead.
1. Right-click the Terminal For AI icon in the Activity Bar
2. Choose Move To
3. Choose Secondary Side Bar

Dragging the icon to the right edge of the window does the same thing. To undo it, right-click the icon again and pick Move To → Side Bar.
walkthrough.setup.move.altText: Right-clicking the Terminal For AI icon in the Activity Bar, then Move To, then Secondary Side Bar
walkthrough.setup.session.title: Start your first session
walkthrough.setup.session.description:
Opening the view starts a shell in the workspace root automatically. Run your AI CLI there and keep the editor for yourself.
[Open Terminal For AI](command:terminal-for-ai-cli.focus)
Up to two sessions run at once — `+` adds the second, `▢` shows both at the same time. Hold Shift while dropping an image on the view to type its path into the shell.
walkthrough.setup.session.altText: The Terminal For AI CLI icon
